m2Definition.definition: A current complete five-digit postcode assignment/exception denominator and fixed Pošta Srbije six-digit PAK Polygon/MultiPolygon release are usable under explicit reviewed AGID processing, derivation, storage, redistribution and public-serving permission. Provider, edition, reference date, licence, attribution, byte length, SHA-256, schema, source CRS, reviewed transform, topology, coverage, exclusions and reproducible conversion are fixed in an approved immutable artifact; any five-digit area derived from PAK is fully reconciled, labelled derived and never relabels PAK as postcode. officialObservations.finding: Pošta defines a postcode as five digits, says one postcode cannot belong to two or more post offices, and defines PAK as six digits identifying part of a street more precisely than a postcode. The identities remain separate.

Pošta directs users to Find a post office/map and explicitly says the postcode database cannot be downloaded electronically. The reviewed ENP PDF is only a sales-point subset and is not a national assignment denominator.

The public tool supports address-to-PAK and PAK-to-address modes. WSP address verification returns a postcode and calculated PAK, but access is for registered users after operator confirmation; documentation is not bulk data authorization or a geometry artifact.

Pošta says it georeferenced over 113,000 PAKs throughout Serbia and that a PAK polygon contains buildings belonging to part of one street. The GIS portal exposes PAK polygon display/search, establishing existence and authority but not a fixed reusable delivery.

The exact one-page price list prices PAK spatial-position data at 90 RSD per data unit before VAT, with quantity discounts. No purchase occurred and no compatible processing, derivation, redistribution or public-serving licence was found on the reviewed public pages.

RGZ advertises weekly street and house-number CSV/GPKG under the Serbian Open Data License. Advertised fields include street/address/cadastral identifiers and point geometry, but not postcode or PAK; address data cannot substitute for postal assignment or a PAK/postcode polygon.
